Statements made in this Annual Report on Form 10-K that are not historical in nature are forward-looking within the meaning of the Private Securities Litigation Reform Act of 1995 and are subject to known and unknown risks, uncertainties and other factors. Horace Mann Educators Corporation (referred to in this Annual Report on Form 10-K as "we", "our", "us", the "Company", "Horace Mann" or "HMEC") is an insurance holding company. We are not under any obligation to (and expressly disclaim any such obligation to) update or revise any forward-looking statements, whether as a result of new information, future events or otherwise. It is important to note that our actual results could differ materially from those projected in forward-looking statements due to a number of risks and uncertainties inherent in our business. See Part I - Item 1A of this Annual Report on Form 10-K for additional information regarding risks and uncertainties.
We are an insurance holding company incorporated in Delaware. Our headquarters is located in Springfield, Ill. We also operate corporate offices in Dallas, Tx., Madison, Wisc., and Cherry Hill, N.J.

Founded by Educators for Educators®, our business began in Springfield in 1945 when two school teachers saw a need to provide automobile insurance to their association members. Horace Mann Educators Corporation (HMEC) was originally named Illinois Education Association (IEA). The Company expanded its business to other states and broadened its product line to include group and individual life insurance in 1949, 403(b) tax-qualified retirement annuities in 1961 and homeowners insurance in 1965.

HMEC was formed as an insurance holding company, and products and services were offered through its subsidiaries, which included: Horace Mann Insurance Company (HMIC), Teachers Insurance Company (TIC), Horace Mann Property & Casualty Insurance Company (HMP) and Horace Mann Life Insurance Company (HML). HMIC, the initial property and casualty insurer, was originally incorporated as the Swiss National Insurance Company, U.S.A. and commenced business on Dec. 23, 1963. The present name, Horace Mann Insurance Company, was adopted on Nov. 2, 1967.

In 1968, INA Corporation (INA), a Philadelphia-based insurance and financial services corporation, acquired a 25% interest in Horace Mann. In 1974, INA began increasing its holdings of Horace Mann and by January 1975 had acquired the entire company. In 1982, INA Corporation merged with Connecticut General Corporation, forming a new holding company known as CIGNA Corporation (CIGNA). In August 1989, an investor group directed by Gibbons, Green, van Amerongen, L.P. (subsequently Gibbons, Goodwin, van Amerongen) (GGvA) and certain members of the Company's senior management acquired what is now known as HMEC from CIGNA.

That newly independent company began trading on the New York Stock Exchange (NYSE) under the symbol HMN following an initial public offering in November 1991. Over the next 30 years, the Company continued to expand its reach into the education market, providing personal line insurance and financial services products. By the mid-2010s, the Company served educators in 47 states.
Horace Mann Educators Corporation Annual Report on Form 10-K 1

In 2019, the Company increased its market share when it acquired all of the equity interests in NTA Life Enterprises, LLC (NTA). NTA provides products and services through its insurance subsidiaries, National Teachers Associates Life Insurance Company (NTALIC) and NTA Life Insurance Company of New York (NTALIC NY). In 2022, we enhanced our value proposition for school districts by acquiring Madison National Life Insurance Company, Inc. (MNL) from its former parent, Independence Holding Company (IHC).

Today, we are proud to be the largest multiline financial services company focused on helping America's educators and others who serve their communities achieve lifelong financial success. Our individual solutions include auto insurance, homeowners insurance, life insurance, retirement solutions and supplemental health insurance. We also provide group benefits for disability, life and supplemental health. We have three reporting segments: Property & Casualty, Life & Retirement, and Supplemental & Group Benefits.

We do not allocate the impact of corporate-level transactions to the three reporting segments, consistent with the basis for management's evaluation of the results of those segments, but classify those items in a separate reporting segment, Corporate & Other.

Our Annual Reports on Form 10-K, Quarterly Reports on Form 10-Q, Current Reports on Form 8-K, Proxy Statements, and all amendments to those reports, are available free of charge through the Investors section of our website, investors.horacemann.com, as soon as reasonably practicable after such reports are filed with or furnished to the Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC). The EDGAR filings of such reports are also available at the SEC's website, www.sec.gov.

Also available in the Investors section of our website are our Corporate Governance Principles, Code of Conduct, Vendor Code of Conduct and other corporate policies as well as the charters of the HMEC Board of Directors (Board), Audit Committee, Compensation Committee, Executive Committee, Investment and Finance Committee and Nominating and Governance Committee. Copies also may be obtained by writing to Investor Relations, Horace Mann Educators Corporation, 1 Horace Mann Plaza, Springfield, Illinois 62715-0001. Our corporate social responsibility (CSR) reporting is available through the CSR section of our website, csr.horacemann.com.

On June 10, 2025, our Chief Executive Officer (CEO) submitted the Annual Section 12(a) CEO Certification to the NYSE without any qualifications. We filed with the SEC, as exhibits to the Annual Report on Form 10-K for the year ended December 31, 2024, the CEO and Chief Financial Officer (CFO) certifications required under Section 302 of the Sarbanes-Oxley Act.

headings: Risks Related to Economic Conditions, Market Conditions and Investments
Volatile financial markets and adverse economic environments can affect financial market risk as well as our financial condition and results of operations.
Changes in interest rates could have a material adverse effect on our financial condition and results of operations.
Our investment portfolios are subject to the risk of loss.

The personal lines insurance, retirement and supplemental group benefit markets are highly competitive and our financial condition and results of operations may be adversely affected by competitive forces.
The development and maintenance of our various distribution channels are critical to growth in product sales and profits.
If we are not able to maintain secure access to educators, our financial condition and results of operations could be adversely affected.
Lack of successful execution on acquisition integration strategies could result in impairment of goodwill and intangible assets that could adversely affect our results of operations.

A catastrophe event, a series of multiple catastrophe events or a series of non-catastrophe severe weather events could have a material adverse effect on our financial condition and results of operations.
Our property and casualty loss reserves may not be adequate.
Our legacy commercial lines exposure could encounter adjustments to loss reserve estimates.
Actual experience differing significantly from our life and health pricing and reserving assumptions could negatively affect our results of operations and financial condition.
A large-scale pandemic, the occurrence of terrorism, or military actions may have an adverse effect on our business.
Climate change may adversely affect our financial position, results of operations, and cash flows.
Cybersecurity breaches could have an adverse effect on our business and reputation.
Successful execution of our business growth strategy is dependent on effective implementation of new or enhanced technology systems and applications.
Loss of key vendor relationships could affect our operations.
Our ability to attract, develop, engage, and retain top talent, maintain optimal staffing levels, and foster/sustain a highly inclusive and engaging culture contributes to our success.
Financial Strength, Credit and Counterparty Risks
Losses due to defaults by others could reduce our profitability or negatively affect the value of our investments.
Uncollectible reinsurance, as well as reinsurance availability and pricing, can have a material adverse effect on our business volume and profitability.
We are subject to the credit risk of our counterparties, including reinsurers who reinsure business from our insurance companies.
Any downgrade in or adverse change in outlook for our claims-paying ratings, financial strength ratings or credit ratings could adversely affect our financial condition and results of operations.
Changes in tax rates, laws or regulations could adversely impact our financial results.
Our business is subject to extensive regulation, which limits our operating flexibility and could negatively impact our financial results.
Legal, statutory and regulatory developments could adversely impact our business by increasing costs or making our business less profitable.
Litigation may harm our financial strength or reduce our profitability.

We have identified what we believe reflect key significant risks to the organization, and in turn to our shareholders, which are outlined below. Any of the risks described below could result in a significant or material adverse effect on our results of operations or financial condition. In addition to these enumerated risks, we face numerous other strategic, operational and emerging risks that could in the aggregate lead to shortfalls to our long-term goals or add to short-term volatility in our earnings. Additionally, many risk factors are correlated, which could exacerbate the financial impact. The disclosures in this section reflect our beliefs and opinions as to factors that could materially and adversely affect us in the future. References to past events are provided by way of example only and are not intended to be a complete listing or a representation as to whether or not such factors have occurred in the past. The following review of important risk factors should not be construed as exhaustive and should be read in conjunction with the Forward-looking Information section located in Part I - Item 1 of this Annual Report on Form 10-K as well as Part II - Item 8, "Financial Statements and Supplementary Data" of this Annual Report on Form 10-K and other reports and materials we submit to the SEC. The words or phrases believe, anticipate, estimate, project, plan, expect, intend, hope, forecast, evaluate, will likely result or will continue or words or phrases of similar import generally involve forward-looking statements. All of the risks that may affect our financial or operating performance may not be material at this time but may become material in the future.

Our business and results of operations are materially affected by conditions in the capital markets and the U.S. economy, as well as by the global economy to the extent it affects the U.S. economy. Actual or perceived stressed conditions, volatility and disruptions in financial asset classes or various capital markets can have an adverse effect on us, both because we have a large investment portfolio and our benefit and claim liabilities are sensitive to changing market factors, including interest rates, credit spreads, derivative prices and availability, and volatility of capital markets. In an economic downturn characterized by higher unemployment and lower family income, the demand for our products could be adversely affected as customers are unwilling or unable to purchase them. In addition, we may experience an elevated incidence of claims, adverse utilization of benefits relative to our best estimate assumptions, and increased lapses or surrenders of policies. Such adverse changes in the economy could negatively affect our earnings and have a material adverse effect on our financial condition, results of operations and our ability to receive dividends from our insurance subsidiaries.

Significant market volatility in reaction to geopolitical risks, changing monetary policy, and uncertain fiscal policy may exacerbate some of the risks we face. Equity and credit market volatility may reduce net investment income from limited partnership interests accounted for using the equity method of accounting, negatively impacting the results of operations. Declining equity markets may also decrease separate account values as well as fixed account values of our retirement products, reducing certain fees generated by these products.

•life insurance, primarily traditional term, whole life, and indexed universal life insurance products

paragraphs: 本年度報表（10-K）中，未依美國通用會計原則（non-GAAP）計算之指標，於本年度報表第一部分首次出現時會標註星號（*）。有關這些指標之說明，請參閱本年度報表（10-K）所附之 Exhibit 99.1「選項術語詞彙表」，並於本公司 2025 年第四季投資者補充資料之附錄中，提供與依美國通用會計原則（GAAP）計算之最直接可比指標之對應說明。

本年度報表（10-K）中，非歷史性之陳述屬「1995 年私人證券訴訟改革法案」所定義之預測性陳述，並受已知及未知風險、不確定性及其他因素影響。Horace Mann Educators Corporation（於本年度報表（10-K）中簡稱為「我們」、「我們的」、「我們」、「本公司」、「Horace Mann」或「HMEC」）為一保險控股公司。我們無義務（並明確否認此義務）更新或修正任何預測性陳述，無論係因新資訊、未來事件或其他因素所致。請注意，我們實際結果可能因業務內在之風險與不確定性而與預測性陳述有重大差異。有關風險與不確定性之更多資訊，請參閱本年度報表（10-K）第一部分第 1A 項。
我們為一於特拉華州註冊之保險控股公司。總部設於伊利諾州史普林菲爾德。我們亦於德克薩斯州達拉斯、威斯康辛州麥迪遜及新澤西州奇利霍克設有分公司。

由教育者為教育者所創立，我們的業務於 1945 年在史普林菲爾德開始，當時兩位教師見到需要為其協會成員提供汽車保險。Horace Mann Educators Corporation（HMEC）原名為伊利諾州教育協會（IEA）。本公司於 1949 年擴展業務至其他州，並於 1949 年擴展產品線，包括團體及個人人壽保險；於 1961 年加入 403(b) 稅優退撫年金；於 1965 年加入房屋保險。

HMEC 設立為一保險控股公司，其產品與服務透過其子公司提供，包括：Horace Mann Insurance Company（HMIC）、Teachers Insurance Company（TIC）、Horace Mann Property & Casualty Insurance Company（HMP）及 Horace Mann Life Insurance Company（HML）。HMIC，為最初的財產與意外保險公司，原為瑞士國家保險公司（Swiss National Insurance Company, U.S.A.）設立，並於 1963 年 12 月 23 日開始營業。現名 Horace Mann Insurance Company 於 1967 年 11 月 2 日正式採用。

1968 年，位於費城之 INA Corporation（INA），一保險與金融服務公司，取得 HMEC 25% 之股權。1974 年，INA 開始增加其在 HMEC 之持股，並於 1975 年 1 月取得 HMEC 全部股權。1982 年，INA Corporation 與 Connecticut General Corporation 合併，成立新之控股公司，名為 CIGNA Corporation（CIGNA）。1989 年 8 月，由 Gibbons, Green, van Amerongen, L.P.（後為 Gibbons, Goodwin, van Amerongen）（GGvA）及本公司高階管理層部分成員所領導之投資者集團，從 CIGNA 收購現為 HMEC 之公司。
該新獨立公司於 1991 年 11 月首次公開發行股票後，在紐約證券交易所（NYSE）以 HMN 編碼上市交易。接下來的 30 年間，本公司持續擴展在教育市場之影響力，提供個人線保險與金融服務產品。至 2010 年代中期，本公司已為 47 個州之教育者提供服務。
Horace Mann Educators Corporation 年度報表（10-K） 1

2019 年，本公司因取得 NTA Life Enterprises, LLC（NTA）全部股權，而提升其市佔率。NTA 透過其人壽子公司 National Teachers Associates Life Insurance Company（NTALIC）及 NTA Life Insurance Company of New York（NTALIC NY）提供產品與服務。2022 年，我們透過取得 Madison National Life Insurance Company, Inc.（MNL）從其原母公司 Independence Holding Company（IHC）以強化學校區的價值主張。
目前，我們為協助美國教育工作者及其他服務社區的人士實現終身財務成功，而自豪地成為專注於多線業務的金融服務公司。我們的個人解決方案包括汽車保險、住宅保險、人壽保險、退休方案及附加健康保險。我們也提供團體福利，包括殘障、人壽及附加健康保險。我們有三個應報告分部：財產與意外險、人壽與退休、以及附加與團體福利。
我們不將公司層級交易的影響分派至這三個應報告分部，與管理階層評估這些分部結果的基礎一致，但將這些項目歸類至一個獨立的應報告分部，即 Corporate & Other。
本公司年度報告書（Form 10-K）、季報（Form 10-Q）、現況報告書（Form 8-K）、股東會資料及所有這些報告的更正資料，均可免費於本公司網站投資者專區（investors.horacemann.com）上，自這些報告提交或提供給證券交易委員會（SEC）後儘速取得。這些報告的 EDGAR 檔案亦可在 SEC 網站（www.sec.gov）取得。

本公司網站投資者專區亦提供本公司企業治理原則、行為準則、供應商行為準則及其他企業政策，以及 HMEC 董事會（董事會）、審計委員會、薪酬委員會、執行委員會、投資與財務委員會及提名與治理委員會的章程。如需紙本複製本，可寫信至投資者關係部門，Horace Mann Educators Corporation，1 Horace Mann Plaza，Springfield，Illinois 62715-0001。本公司企業社會責任（CSR）報告書可於網站 CSR 專區（csr.horacemann.com）取得。
2025 年 6 月 10 日，本公司首席執行長（CEO）已向紐約證券交易所（NYSE）提交年度 Section 12(a) CEO 證明書，且無任何保留意見。本公司已將依薩班斯-奧克斯利法案第 302 條所要求的 CEO 及首席財務長（CFO）證明書，作為年度報告書（Form 10-K）之附屬文件，提交至 SEC。

HMEC為一保險控股公司，專注於協助美國教育工作者及其他服務社區之人士實現終身財務成功。透過我們之子公司，我們行銷與承保個別與團體保險及財務解決方案，以符合教育界之需求，包括：
•個人財產與意外保險業務，主要為汽車與財產保險 •退休產品，主要為符合稅收資格的固定、變額及固定收益型年金
•人壽保險，主要為傳統定期、終身及指數型萬能壽險產品
Horace Mann Educators Corporation 年度報告書（10-K 表格）第 41 頁
•個人附加保險產品，包括意外、癌症、重大疾病、醫院及附加殘障保險
•團體福利保險產品，主要為團體殘障、團體人壽及團體附加醫療保險
我們主要將產品行銷給 K-12 教師、行政人員及其他公立學校員工及其家庭，無論他們是直接與 Horace Mann 互動或透過其學區/僱主，以及其他服務社區的羣體。

波動的財務市場與不利的經濟環境可能影響財務市場風險以及本公司的財務狀況與營運成果。
利率變動可能對本公司的財務狀況與營運成果產生重大不利影響。
本公司投資組合面臨資產減損的風險。
個人保險、退休及補充團體福利市場競爭激烈，本公司財務狀況與營運成果可能因競爭壓力而受到不利影響。
本公司各項分銷通路之開發與維護，對產品銷售與獲利之成長至關重要。
若本公司無法維持對教育工作者之安全存取，將可能對財務狀況及營運結果產生不利影響。
未能成功執行收購整合策略，可能導致商譽及無形資產減損，進而對營運結果產生不利影響。
災難事件、一系列多起災難事件或一系列非災難性嚴重天氣事件，可能對財務狀況及營運結果產生重大不利影響。
本公司財產及意外保險之損失備抵可能不足。
本公司傳統商業業務之風險敞口，可能遭遇對損失備抵估計之調整。
實際經驗與本公司壽險及健康險之定價及備抵假設有顯著差異，可能對營運結果及財務狀況產生負面影響。
一場大規模的疫情、恐怖攻擊事件或軍事行動可能對本公司業務產生不利影響。
氣候變遷可能對本公司財務狀況、營運成果及現金流產生不利影響。
網路安全事件的發生可能對本公司業務及聲譽產生不利影響。
本公司業務成長策略的成功執行，依賴於新或增強的科技系統及應用程式之有效實施。
關鍵供應商關係的喪失可能影響本公司營運。
本公司吸引、培養、激勵及留住頂尖人才、維持最佳人力配置，並培育/維持高度包容性與參與感的文化，對本公司成功具有重要貢獻。
財務強度、信用及交易對手風險
因他人違約所導致的損失可能降低本公司利潤或對本公司投資價值產生負面影響。
無法收回的再保險、再保險可得性及價格，可能對我們的業務規模及獲利能力產生重大不利影響。
我們面臨對手方的信用風險，包括再保險公司，這些再保險公司為我們的保險公司再保險業務。
我們的理賠支付等級、財務強度等級或信用等級若遭降級或展望出現不利變動，可能對我們的財務狀況及營運成果產生不利影響。
稅率、法律或法規的變動，可能對我們的財務結果產生不利影響。
我們的業務面臨嚴格的法規監管，這會限制我們的營運彈性，並可能對我們的財務結果產生負面影響。
法律、法定及法規的發展，可能對我們的業務產生不利影響，例如增加成本或使我們的業務較不獲利。
訴訟可能損害我們的財務強度或降低我們的獲利能力。
paragraphs: 頁面導讀 經濟條件、市場條件與投資相關風險 戰略風險
運營風險 財務強度、信用與交易對手風險 註冊與法律風險

我們已識別出我們認為反映對組織、以及對我們股東而言具有重大影響的風險，並在下文列出。任何上述所描述的風險都可能導致對我們營運結果或財務狀況產生重大或具體的不利影響。除了這些明確列出的風險外，我們還面臨許多其他戰略、運營及新興風險，這些風險總體上可能導致我們長期目標的落差，或增加我們短期獲利的波動。此外，許多風險因素是相關的，這可能會加劇財務影響。本節的披露反映我們對未來可能對我們產生重大且不利影響的因素的信念與觀點。對過去事件的參考僅為範例，並非完整清單，也不代表這些因素是否在過去已經發生。以下對重要風險因素的審視不應被視為詳盡，應與本年度報告表10-K第I部第1項「前瞻性資訊」以及第II部第8項「財務報表與補充資料」以及我們提交給SEC的其他報告與資料一併閱讀。詞語或短語如「相信」、「預期」、「估計」、「預測」、「計畫」、「期望」、「意圖」、「希望」、「預測」、「評估」、「很可能導致」或「將持續」等，通常涉及前瞻性陳述。所有可能影響我們財務或營運表現的風險，目前可能並不具重大性，但未來可能變得重大。

我們的業務與營運結果受到資本市場條件與美國經濟，以及全球經濟（若影響美國經濟）的影響。實際或被認為的壓力條件、財務資產類別或各個資本市場的波動與動盪，可能對我們產生不利影響，這是因為我們擁有龐大的投資組合，而我們的福利與賠償負債對市場因素的變化非常敏感，包括利率、信用 spreads、衍生品價格與可得性，以及資本市場的波動性。在以高失業率和低家庭收入為特徵的經濟衰退中，對我們產品的需求可能受到不利影響，因為客戶可能不願或無法購買這些產品。此外，我們可能經歷較高的聲請數量、與我們最佳估計假設相比的福利使用率惡化，以及保單的增加解約或贖回。這些經濟的不利變化可能對我們的獲利產生負面影響，並對我們的財務狀況、營運結果以及我們從保險子公司獲取紅利的能力產生重大不利影響。
因應地緣政治風險、貨幣政策的變化及財政政策的不確定性而產生的重大市場波動，可能加劇我們所面臨的一些風險。股權與信用市場的波動可能減少以權益法會計處理的有限合夥權益投資所產生的淨投資收入，對營運結果產生負面影響。股權市場的下跌也可能降低我們退休產品的分離賬戶價值以及固定賬戶價值，進而減少這些產品所產生的某些費用。
Horace Mann Educators Corporation 年度報告表10-K 23
